study protocol description: Jurkat T cells (ATCC Manassas, USA, Clone E6-1, TIB152) were cultured in RPMI 1640 (Biochrom, Berlin, Germany Cat. Nr FG1215) medium, supplemented with 10% FCS and 1% Pen/Strep. Split every second day.

For the centrifugation study (300× g 5 min), 5 mL of 1 × 10^6 cells/mL Jurkat T cells was used that had not been exposed to centrifugation for 48 h. Four control samples were directly fixed. Three times four samples were centrifuged at 300× g for 5 min and fixed after one minute after centrifuge stop (fastest that was realistically possible while keeping experimental standard), after four minutes and after 15 min. The centrifuge stop time was 8.34 s (7.95 s–8.67 s min/max), therefore corresponding to 2.7% (5 min time point) of the total centrifugation time. The four heat shock samples were inserted into a 42 C water bath under constant rotation to ensure mixing. The temperature curve was previously recorded: After one minute, the liquid was at 40 C, from then on five minutes of heat exposure was performed before addition of RLT buffer to immediately stop all reactions.
Immediately after centrifugation, samples were eluted into RLT buffer.
Total RNA was extracted by QIAGEN RNeasy Mini-Kits (Hilden, Germany).

OSD-999.study description: This study aims to characterize transcriptomic responses to Simplified 5 Ion GCR Simulation (simGCRsim) in human brain organoids derived from hiPSCs. Two independent RNA-seq experiments were conducted. The first set compared male- and female-derived organoids to evaluate sex-specific transcriptional responses to GCR. The second set assessed organoids derived from i) male hiPSCs expressing optogenetically-controlled FGFR (opto-FGFR) or mock constructs to explore FGFR signaling as a potential countermeasure and ii) one female hiPSC line (SC2131), with or without GCR exposure. Together, these datasets provide insight into both intrinsic sex differences and FGFR-dependent protective mechanisms in human neural tissues in the context of space radiation exposure. This study host the data of the sex-specific response experiment, and the data of Opto-FGFR-mediated rescue under simGCRsim exposure is available in OSD-1000.

study protocol description: Cell lines: Healthy male (CS25, BC1, SC1014, SC1015, KOLF2.1J, ApoE, and CS0002) and female (H9, SC2131, 0 1582, 0 2623, CS83iCTR, CS0201) hiPSC and embryonic stem cell (ESC) lines were cultured on mitotically inactivated mouse embryonic fibroblasts (Gibco), in hESC medium containing DMEM/F-12 supplemented with 20% knockout serum replacement (KSR), 0.1 mM minimum essential medium-nonessential amino acids (MEM-NEAA), 2 mM L-glutamine, 55 uM beta-mercaptoethanol (all from Life Technologies) and 10 ng/mL FGF2 (R and D Systems). Culture media were refreshed daily. Cells were maintained at 37 C and 5% CO2 in a humidified incubator and regularly tested for mycoplasma contamination.

Generation of Cortical Brain Organoids: Cortical brain organoids were generated from hiPSCs as previously described. Briefly, hiPSCs were dissociated into single cells using TrypLE, and 5.0 × 10^5 cells were seeded per well in ultra-low attachment U-bottom 96-well plates (Corning) to form uniform aggregates in mTeSR Plus medium (STEMCELL Technologies) supplemented with 50 uM Y-27632 (BioGems). On day 2, two-thirds of the medium was replaced every other day with fresh mTeSR Plus medium lacking Y-27632. When aggregates reached a diameter of 350 - 450 um, each aggregate was transferred to 24-well plates (Corning) containing cortical induction medium [DMEM/F12, N2 (1:200), B27 (1:100), 0.2 mg/mL glucose, 0.15 ug/mL cAMP, 0.5% NEAA, 1% L-alanyl-Lglutamine, 10 ug/mL heparin, 180 nM LDN-193189, 500 nM A83-01, 10 ug/mL IWR-1] and maintained for 4–5 days. Medium was changed every 3 days. Upon neuroectodermal differentiation, as indicated by brightened aggregate surfaces and radial neuroepithelial morphology, aggregates were embedded in growth factor-reduced Geltrex (Thermo Fisher Scientific) droplets. Geltrex-embedded aggregates were transferred to low-attachment 6-cm petri dishes containing organoid differentiation medium [DMEM-F12 with N2 supplement (1:200), B27 supplement (1:100), glucose (0.2 mg/mL), cAMP (0.15 ug/mL), 0.5% NEAA, 1% L-alanylL-glutamine, insulin (2.5 ug/mL)]. Media were refreshed every 3–4 days, and organoids were cultured on an orbital shaker to promote maturation. After 2 months of maturation, organoids were transported to NSRL and exposed to simGCRsim.

To model GCR exposure, a simGCRsim incorporating a composition of ions and energies based on NASA’s consensus profile for exploratory space missions was utilized. The radiation included 1000 MeV protons, 600 MeV/n 28Si, 250 MeV/n 4He, 350 MeV/n 16O, 600 MeV/n 56Fe, and 250 MeV protons. These particles were administered in the following proportions: Protons 1000 MeV at 35.0%,Si at 1.0%, He at 18%, O at 6.0%, 56Fe at 1.0%, and Protons 250 MeV at 39.0%. This formulation, known as simGCRsim, serves as a practical representation of the radiation environment encountered during long-duration spaceflight. NSRL GCR and SPE simulations are designed to approximate the chronic mixed field exposures in space by means of sequential acute exposures to a variety of ion/energy combinations.
The exposure protocols are on the NSRL website: https://www.bnl.gov/nsrl/userguide/simgcrsim.php (SimGCRSim).
The dose can be administered either in a single series of exposures lasting approximately an hour or in daily fractions over several weeks.

The GCR simulations are described in detail here: Simonsen LC, Slaba TC, Guida P, Rusek A (2020) NASA’s first ground-based Galactic Cosmic Ray Simulator: Enabling a new era in space radiobiology research. PLoS Biol 18(5): e3000669. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pbio.3000669

After irradiation, organoids were returned to standard culture conditions and harvested 48 hours post-exposure for RNA extraction. For RNA-seq and flow cytometry, brain organoids were enzymatically dissociated into single cells using papain (STEMCELL Technologies) according to the manufacturer’s instructions (https://www.stemcell.com/how-to-dissociate-3dneural-organoids-into-single-cell-suspension.html).

Total RNA was extracted from brain organoids using the miRNeasy Mini kit (Qiagen), according to the manufacturer’s protocol. RNA integrity and concentration were assessed using
an Agilent Bioanalyzer.
